site.name: Master Video Styles
site.note: New site (not the ireels library). Styles are summarized in plain words from the source playbooks; reference reel URLs and creator handles are kept exact.
site.tagline: Every video style, mastered — pick a style, post your raw footage, get a video back.

styles.best_for: Explainers, lessons, talking-head teaching videos — anything that teaches one idea well.
styles.creator: Sumit
styles.look: The speaker stays on camera the whole time. Every idea they speak gets a visual: a keyword in big animated text plus a simple illustration of the metaphor. One colour runs through the whole video — pink in the reference reel. Fast and clean, never boring.
styles.prompt: Edit this footage in the Sumit style: the speaker stays on screen the whole time, one colour theme for the whole video, one visual per spoken beat (a kinetic-text keyword plus a simple icon of the metaphor), fast clean pacing with no dead air, keywords big and bold animated exactly on the beat.
styles.reference_reel_note: "Claude vs Human Creativity" — the same talking-head clip edited three ways. The human edit is the target; the Claude edit in the same reel is what NOT to copy.
rules: Speaker stays on screen. Graphics support them, they never replace them.
One colour theme per video. Backgrounds, text, icons and illustrations all live in that one palette.

One visual per spoken beat. Every idea gets a kinetic-text keyword plus a simple icon of the metaphor (brain = overthinking, shield = protection, compass or target = goals). No visual without a spoken reason behind it.
Fast, clean pacing. A new visual on nearly every beat. No dead air, no empty talking-head stretches.
Real photos only when they prove something — a diploma, a book cover, a result.
Keywords big, bold, animated in exactly on the beat of the word being spoken.
Documentary tone: clear, confident, educational. Never cheesy, never cluttered.

steps.detail: Study the raw talking head, write the opening hook, sync the speaking audio, pick the emphasis words, and set the theme: one glow colour, scattered typography, stark grayscale background shifts.
steps.title: Hook & setup

steps.detail: Cut the speaker out of the background with Roto Brush. Add an animated neon outline in the theme colour around their exact silhouette. Keyframe the background from the natural room to stark white or grayscale. Clean mask edges around hair and hands.
steps.title: Masking & roto

steps.detail: Secondary footage for multi-cam sequences (driving, lounging, walking outdoors). Picture-in-picture collages with drop shadows, several clips on screen at once. Prep 3D assets for metaphor cues (e.g. a dartboard icon for discipline).
steps.title: B-roll & picture-in-picture

steps.detail: Bold text popping word by word, synced to the speaker's pacing. Scattered-text effect for key phrases, words placed randomly across the screen. Mixed fonts: serif for accents, clean sans-serif for subtitles. Alternate theme colour and white. Scale bounces and rotational keyframes for energy.
steps.title: Kinetic typography

steps.detail: Whooshes for collage slide-ins, a pop or click on every kinetic word reveal. Balance voiceover EQ so sound effects never overpower speech. Warm colour grade in the theme colour, natural skin tones kept.
steps.title: Sound & colour polish

steps.detail: Final playback check that text and collages are perfectly timed. Apply revisions. Export H.264 MP4 optimised for social. Back up project files to the cloud.
steps.title: Review & export

styles.title: The Sumit Style

styles.best_for: Tips lists, checklists, real estate, any "X things to know" video.
styles.creator: Kelsie Blevins
styles.look: A numbered list, fired fast. A promise plus a visible clock: "everything you need to know in under 30 seconds" with a ticking countdown timer on screen the whole time. Twelve tips in about 35 seconds, one big keyword flashing per tip.
styles.prompt: Edit this footage in the Kelsie listicle style: a numbered rapid-fire list with a visible 30-second countdown timer on screen the whole time, about 3 seconds per tip, one big animated keyword phrase per tip (short phrases only, never full sentences), ending with a "Save this for later" card plus a contact call to action. Also write the full numbered-list caption.
styles.reference_reel_note: "Thinking about selling? Here's everything you need to know in under 30 seconds." 12 seller tips, seated talking head, visible countdown timer.
rules: The hook is a promise plus a visible clock. Open with "everything you need to know in under 30 seconds" and keep a countdown timer on screen the whole video — the ticking clock is the pressure that keeps people watching.
Numbered rapid-fire list. 12 tips in about 35 seconds, roughly 3 seconds per tip. One numbered badge per tip, counting up on screen as the list runs.
Animated keyword text overlays on every tip. Short phrases only ("Don't overprice", "Marketing Plan", "Strategy") — big, bold, popping in on the beat. Never full sentences on screen.
Seated talking head, direct to camera, bright clean interior. The speaker is the authority — confident, instructional, promotional.
One idea per tip, no rambling. Cut ruthlessly: if a tip takes more than one sentence to say, it is two tips or it gets cut.
End card with two calls to action: "Save this for later" and the contact CTA (DM / call). The save prompt is the point — it is what makes the reel spread.
Caption carries the full numbered list so the video works even on mute and people save it as a checklist.

steps.detail: Pick 12 tips. One sentence each, one idea each. If a tip needs two sentences, split it or cut it.
steps.title: Write the list

steps.detail: Put a visible 30-second countdown timer on screen for the whole video. It is the hook.
steps.title: Set the clock

steps.detail: Bright, clean interior. Confident delivery, about 3 seconds per tip.
steps.title: Film seated, direct to camera

steps.detail: A counting badge per tip, plus one big animated keyword phrase per tip — short phrases only.
steps.title: Add numbered badges and keywords

steps.detail: End card: "Save this for later" plus the contact CTA. Write the full numbered list into the caption as a checklist.
steps.title: End card and caption

styles.title: The Kelsie Listicle

styles.best_for: Selling a home, listing tours, property walkthroughs.
styles.creator: Kelsie Blevins
styles.look: A lifestyle-first home tour: sell where you live before what you buy. One unbroken camera flight from the street into the rooms, an aerial of the neighbourhood, then room by room — one selling point each, no lingering — and an AI clip where the house turns and changes its look.
styles.prompt: Edit this listing tour in the Kelsie Wilmore format: lifestyle hook in the neighbourhood first, then one unbroken fly-through push-in zoom from the exterior into the interior, an aerial skyline shot, room by room with one selling point each, an AI home-transformation clip where the house turns and changes look, and close seated inside with the investment line plus a comment-word call to action.
styles.reference_reel_note: 2232 Wilmore Dr, Charlotte — $649,950 all-brick bungalow, 3 bed / 2 bath / 1,504 sqft. 53-second listing tour (Nov 16, 2026).

steps.detail: Open walking through the neighbourhood (market, coffee in hand): "What if this? and this? minutes from your door." Sell where you live before what you buy.
steps.title: Hook on lifestyle first, not the house

steps.detail: The camera zooms from the exterior straight into the interior in one continuous move — street to front door to rooms, no cut. That single unbroken push is what makes the house feel big and the tour feel premium. Recreate with a drone or gimbal push-in, or a zoom transition in the edit.
steps.title: Fly-through push-in zoom

steps.detail: One wide drone shot over the area (skyline, trees, streets) right after the hook, before the house itself.
steps.title: Aerial skyline shot

steps.detail: Best feature per room, no lingering. Porch piece-to-camera ("this is where you want to be"), kitchen, open living and dining, bedrooms, then backyard + deck + fire pit. One selling point per room, then move on.
steps.title: Room-by-room tour

steps.detail: An AI-generated shot where the house turns and rotates while its look changes — a restyle or renovation morph. Generate with an AI video tool (Runway, Kling, Higgsfield, Luma): image-to-video turntable of the house, then morph its style or era. It is the "wow" beat of the tour.
steps.title: AI home transformation clip

steps.detail: Close seated inside the home: "If location is everything in real estate, this one is a smart investment" — plus a comment-word CTA ("Comment WILMORE for more info").
steps.title: Close with the investment line

styles.best_for: Pitching a vision for a property or place; redevelopment ideas; getting a community talking about what a site could become.
styles.creator: Melissa Orta
styles.creator_role: Broker Associate, Marzucco Real Estate — Lehigh Acres, FL
styles.look: The agent stands on the site itself and pitches what it could become. Drone footage shows the empty lot as it is today; AI renders laid over the aerial show the future complex. The video ends by asking viewers what they would want to see there.
styles.prompt: Edit this footage in the Melissa vision-pitch style: open on location direct to camera with the "if this were my property" hook, cut to a drone aerial of the current site as the before, overlay AI renders on the aerial showing the envisioned transformation as the after, name each concept with one short on-screen label, then return to the ground and ask viewers what they would want to see there, and close with the branding logo.
styles.reference_reel_note: "If this were my property" — 27-second pitch for a vacant Lehigh Acres property (Nov 10, 2026).

steps.detail: Stand on the site itself and open with the "if this were mine" line ("If this were my property, I'd knock it down and start over"). The speaker is the vision, not a narrator.
steps.title: Hook on location, direct to camera

steps.detail: Wide shot of the empty or vacant property (industrial buildings, cracked lots) so the viewer feels the wasted potential.
steps.title: Drone aerial of the current site — the before

steps.detail: AI-generated visuals laid over the drone shot showing the transformed complex: a coffee shop with big windows and outdoor seating, a brunch spot next door, an Italian restaurant for date night. The render is the wow beat — the same trick as the Kelsie AI home transformation, applied to a whole development instead of one house.
steps.title: AI-render overlay on the aerial — the after

steps.detail: One short label per idea, appearing on the beat you say it — never a paragraph on screen.
steps.title: Name each concept on screen

steps.detail: Gesture at the open space and ask viewers what they would want to see there. The question is the engagement engine — it turns a pitch into a conversation in the comments.
steps.title: Return to the ground and ask the question

steps.detail: No hard sell, no phone number on screen — the authority and the question do the work.
steps.title: Close with the branding logo

styles.title: The Melissa Vision Pitch

styles.best_for: Making any talking-head reel more watchable, fast — five small changes, no reshoot.
styles.creator: Romina Aminian
styles.look: Five small, intentional choices that make a video clearer and easier to follow. Try one or two per video rather than all five at full intensity — the goal is to support what you're saying, not distract from it.
styles.prompt: Apply Romina's 5 easy edits to this reel: pair two complementary fonts and treat text like a graphic, insert a blank colour screen between clips as a visual reset, match the music to the video's energy, add sound effects on transitions and key movements sparingly, and layer simple zooms and text animations.
styles.reference_reel_note: "5 easy edits for instant engagement" — 43-second talking-head tutorial with on-screen numbered graphics (Nov 15, 2026). Companion Notion guide: The Reels Editing Style Swipe File.

steps.detail: Use two complementary fonts with distinct roles: a bold display font for important words, a clean readable font for smaller explanations. Treat text like a graphic — place it where it works with the shot (beside your face, near the object, in negative space). Keep essential text away from Instagram's interface areas.
steps.title: Font pairing & placement

steps.detail: Instead of cutting straight from one talking-head shot to another, insert a full-screen solid colour with a short line of text. A brief visual reset that helps a key sentence land.
steps.title: Blank colour screen

steps.detail: Pick music that fits the video's energy — the track should carry the same feeling as the message, not fight it.
steps.title: Music that matches the energy

steps.detail: Add SFX on transitions, text reveals and key movements — but don't overdo it. A few well-placed sounds beat a noisy edit.
steps.title: Sound effects, sparingly

steps.detail: Simple zooms, text animations and subtle transitions. Small movement keeps the eye engaged without a full rebuild of the edit.
steps.title: Simple zooms & animations

styles.title: Romina's 5 Easy Edits

styles.best_for: Anyone mastering a style end to end — the full 7-day production plan behind a Sumit-style edit.
styles.creator: Overstimulated Mind edit process
styles.creator_role: 6 steps, 7 days — the build process behind the Sumit style
styles.look: The real production process behind a polished talking-head edit: hook and setup, masking and roto, B-roll collages, kinetic type, sound and colour polish, review and export. Seven days, start to finish. This is what "mastering a style" actually means.
styles.prompt: Plan this video with the Overstimulated Mind 6-step process: hook and setup on day 0–1, masking and roto on day 1–2, B-roll and picture-in-picture collages on day 2–3, kinetic typography on day 3–5, sound and colour polish on day 5–6, review and export on day 6–7.
styles.reference_reel_note: Process source: the Overstimulated Mind edit process (Veronika talking head — laziness, discipline, phone, overstimulated mind).

steps.detail: Analyse the raw talking-head footage to craft the opening hook. Set up the timeline and frame rate, sync the original speaking audio. Identify the emphasis words in the script. Establish the visual theme: one glow colour, scattered typography, stark grayscale background shifts.
steps.title: Hook & setup

steps.detail: Isolate the speaker from the background with Roto Brush. Apply the signature animated neon outline around the exact silhouette. Keyframe the background from the natural room to stark white or grayscale. Clean mask edges around hair and hands during fast movements.
steps.title: Masking & roto

steps.detail: Gather and trim secondary footage (driving, lounging, walking outdoors) for multi-cam sequences. Design picture-in-picture collages: several clips on screen at once, with drop shadows. Extract and prep 3D assets for metaphor cues (e.g. a dartboard icon for discipline).
steps.title: B-roll & PiP collages

steps.detail: Animate bold text popping up word by word, synced to the speaker's pacing. Scattered-text effect for key phrases, words placed randomly across the screen. Varied fonts: serif for accents, clean sans-serif for subtitles. Alternate theme colour and white. Scale bounces and rotational keyframes for energy.
steps.title: Kinetic typography

steps.detail: Whooshes for collage slide-ins, distinct pops and clicks for every kinetic word reveal. Balance voiceover EQ with the sound design — SFX never overpower speech. Warm colour grade, natural skin tones kept.
steps.title: SFX & colour polish

steps.detail: Final playback review: rapid text animations and PiP collages perfectly timed. Apply revisions. Export H.264 MP4 optimised for social. Organise project files and back up to the cloud.
steps.title: Review & export

styles.best_for: Launch reels for software and AI products; app promos; product demos.
styles.creator: MotionSmith
styles.creator_role: AI motion design MCP + Claude Code skill
styles.look: One accent colour, neutral grotesk type, UI pieces that morph into each other, a camera that rides one continuous space, and sound effects only — no music. Built from 17 analysed reference reels.
styles.prompt: Use MotionSmith to make my video in the "saas-launch" style.
styles.reference_reel_note: MotionSmith SaaS Launch style — one of two complete looks in the MotionSmith style library. Site: motionsmith.miftahul.com.
rules: Give Claude a reference video plus screen recordings of the product; it breaks the reference down frame by frame and writes a storyboard for approval before building.
Motion design first, sound effects after approval — get the movement right, then add SFX.
Never overwrite a rendered version — notes become the next version, the final goes in a separate folder.
SFX sit 8–15 dB under the voice; mix around -13 LUFS for social.

steps.detail: Hand Claude the reference video, screen recordings of the product, and your prompt. It studies the reference frame by frame and writes a storyboard (around 10 beats) for you to approve.
steps.title: Plan: reference + storyboard

steps.detail: Generate the images and voice-over (ElevenLabs), save them with exact file names. Transcribe the voice-over with Whisper for word timings so animations land on the spoken words.
steps.title: Assets: images, voice, timings

steps.detail: Claude writes the scenes as code (shared helpers, then one file per beat) and renders with a headless browser. Motion first; sound design only after you approve the motion.
steps.title: Build: scenes as code, render

steps.detail: Watch the preview, give notes on timing, words and sounds. Notes become the next version. Final render goes in a separate folder.
steps.title: Review loop

styles.look: A documentary-style collage explainer with layered paper textures, cutout characters, newspaper clippings and subtle shadows — built without manually animating every frame. The project stays an editable timeline in InVideo.
styles.prompt: Create a cinematic paper-cutout collage explainer video about [YOUR TOPIC]. Use my reference images to match the visual style: layered paper textures, cutout characters, subtle shadows, and smooth collage-style animation. Build the project in InVideo Editor as an editable timeline where supported, with separate visual layers, text, transitions, and audio. Keep the pacing engaging, the visuals consistent, and the storytelling clear. First outline the scenes, then create the video project and provide the editor link if the workflow supports it. rules: Gather paper textures, cutout characters, newspaper clippings and backgrounds first — tell Claude which references matter most.
Ask Claude to outline the scenes before it builds anything.

styles.best_for: Building the Sumit style (roto, kinetic type, PiP collages) with Claude doing the After Effects work.
styles.creator: Community bridges (no official Adobe MCP)
styles.creator_role: Claude Code / Claude Desktop, local only
styles.look: Claude talks directly to After Effects on your computer and builds the edit — layers, keyframes, effects and text — all editable afterwards. There is no official Adobe After Effects MCP; every live route is a community bridge, and Claude must run on the same machine as After Effects. Claude on the web cannot reach desktop After Effects.
styles.prompt: Use the After Effects MCP with Claude Code to build this edit in After Effects: layers, keyframes, easing, effects and text, all editable afterwards. If the MCP is not connected, tell me which one to connect instead of guessing or silently switching tools.
styles.reference_reel_note: Researched Nov 17, 2026. Adobe previewed native local MCP for After Effects (Nov 10, 2026) but it is private beta planned for early 2027 and not publicly installable.
rules: Claude must run on the same computer as After Effects (Claude Code or Claude Desktop locally).
Turn on After Effects preference "Allow Scripts to Write Files and Access Network" where required.
MotionSmith does NOT use After Effects — it renders in the browser. It is a separate route.
InVideo MCP only drives InVideo's editor, not After Effects.

steps.detail: Claude Code plugin or standalone MCP. Builds layers, keyframes, easing, effects, expressions and text — all editable afterwards. After Effects 2022+. Needs Node 22+. No render queue tools.

styles.best_for: Showing off a shop, supermarket, showroom or any physical place; a calm, polished tour that lets the space sell itself.
styles.creator: Marché Ariya
styles.creator_role: Supermarché — BBQ au Charbon, Greenfield Park / La Prairie, QC
styles.look: A 30–40 second vertical store tour with no presenter and no voiceover. It opens on a Google Earth-style satellite view that zooms all the way down to the storefront, then glides through about ten departments in slow 2–4 second shots — meat, produce, bulk bins, spices, bakery, tagines — each still moving on a gimbal-smooth push-in or aisle track. One address overlay, one logo watermark, one continuous music bed.
styles.prompt: Edit this footage in the Ariya store-tour style: shoot vertical 9:16; open with a Google Earth-style satellite zoom that descends continuously for about 8 seconds to the storefront, fading in the address in bold white sans-serif inside a thin white frame mid-zoom; then hard-cut through 10–12 departments in 2–4 second shots, each gliding on a slow push-in, pan or forward aisle track; keep a small circular logo watermark at bottom-centre; add one zoom-blur swoop and one brief outlined highlight on a hero product; close on a full-frame logo sign, then dim to black; one continuous instrumental music bed, no voiceover, no subtitles, no end-card text.
styles.reference_reel_note: Marché Ariya store tour — 30–40 second supermarket tour, no presenter, no voiceover (Jul 10, 2024). Watched in full in the live browser Nov 18, 2026.
rules: No presenter, no voiceover — the space is the star.
Every shot keeps moving — slow push-in, gentle pan or forward aisle track, gimbal-smooth, no handheld shake.
One text overlay only: the address. Everything else readable is physical in-store signage.

steps.detail: Vertical portrait, daylight inside and out; warm interior light, saturated colour (turquoise sky, red signage, colourful produce).
steps.title: Shoot vertical 9:16

steps.detail: Google Earth-style high aerial of the street grid, descending continuously for about 8 seconds through a thin cloud layer to the store. Fade the address in bold white sans-serif inside a thin white frame at 2–4 seconds; remove it before landing.
steps.title: Open with the satellite zoom

steps.detail: Low oblique drone shot of the storefront, then a straight-on front view of the entrance for 2–3 seconds.
steps.title: Land on the storefront

steps.detail: Hard-cut through 10–12 departments in 2–4 second shots: dining area, meat/deli, produce, bulk bins, spices, counter, oil/sauce, bakery, tagines, wide aisle tracks. Every shot keeps moving — slow push-in, gentle pan or forward track.
steps.title: Glide through the departments

steps.detail: Small circular logo watermark at bottom-centre through the interior, semi-transparent. Absent from the opening zoom.
steps.title: Keep the watermark on

steps.detail: One fast radial zoom-blur swoop (over the bulk bins) and one brief outlined highlight on a hero product — the tagine fills the frame with a thin bright-blue outline/glow for under a second, then cuts to it on the shelf.
steps.title: Add the two flourish moves

steps.detail: Full-frame close-up of the countertop logo sign, then a dimmed exterior shot fading toward black. No call-to-action, no hours, phone or website on screen.
steps.title: Close on the logo

steps.detail: One continuous instrumental track underneath the whole tour. No voiceover, no dialogue, no subtitles. Track unidentified — pick any unobtrusive instrumental bed.
steps.title: Lay the music bed

tools.notes: Inspect and edit the open composition, preview changes, save an editable .aep. After Effects 2024–2026, Node 24+.

tools.name: Higgsfield bridge
tools.notes: Claude generates images and video, then builds and renders the After Effects composition. Also drives Premiere Pro and Blender. After Effects 2025+.

tools.name: AE GPT
tools.notes: Claude Code running inside After Effects. Saved in the library as vid_291.

tools.name: MotionSmith
tools.notes: Motion-graphics videos in two styles: SaaS Launch and Vox Explainer. Renders in the browser, not in After Effects.

tools.name: Bang Motion
tools.notes: Turns Claude Code into a motion designer — openers, promos, product demos, kinetic typography.

tools.name: motionmaxxing
tools.notes: Rebuilds flat AI videos as polished motion-designer films, rendered locally from plain HTML.

tools.name: line-art-animation
tools.notes: Hand-inked line-art SVG animations — walking figures, day-to-night scenes — rendered as video.

tools.name: Vibha caption styles
tools.notes: Animated captions timed to your voice, burned into the video. Pop Sticker, Paper Plane, Smoke Exit and 4 more.

tools.name: claude-video-effects
tools.notes: 45 talking-head effects in Claude Code — face tracking, layers kept behind your head.

tools.name: AutoEdit (Premiere Pro)
tools.notes: Voice mode in Claude × Premiere Pro. Cuts bad takes, removes silences, builds rough cuts in seconds.

tools.name: DaVinci Resolve MCP
tools.notes: Connects DaVinci Resolve Studio to Claude: 52 tools for timelines, colour grading, Fusion and rendering.

tools.name: Tesseract
tools.notes: Edits the real project, not a re-generated clip — change the captions and only the captions change.

tools.name: InVideo MCP
tools.notes: Claude drives InVideo's editor: describe the ad and it builds it. Paper-cutout collage workflow included in the playbooks.

tools.name: Remotion / HyperFrames
tools.notes: Make videos with React code. Perfect for templated videos that change text each time.

tools.notes: Full 3D suite for product visuals and animated explainers.
